correctness.rationale: The survival-based hazard formula is explicitly normalized. Differentiation yields an exact numerator with sign \(Q(y)-\lambda^2\). A degree-five polynomial with strictly positive coefficients proves \(Q'/Q>2/y\) and hence unique global minimum and globally strict decline of its age across \(\lambda\). Series inversion yields the two endpoint age, hazard-depth and mean-lifetime-ratio formulas. Every boundary is treated as a limit, not an included parameter. The standalone script reproduced 136 symbolic/numerical checks; finite checks do not replace this proof.

value.rationale: The age attaining minimum instantaneous failure hazard is a standard reliability object, but the linked LR1 weight and component-rate response creates two distinct and quantitatively sharp regimes. A globally decreasing absolute minimum age is coupled with a normalized age crossing from \(o(1)\) to a logarithmically diverging number of mean lifetimes. Exact constants and a log-log correction characterize the precise model used by the motivating publication. Neither uniqueness alone nor routine algebra is offered as the novelty/value argument. No cost-optimal policy is inferred.
